# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Refactored microfauna feeding to follow the closed-loop consumer routing contract (docs/ROUTING.md). Previously, microfauna consumed periphyton and detritus and routed all material directly to dissolved organics (DON/DOC), skipping fecal, respiration, and excretion pathways. Now microfauna use the same routing template as shrimp: ingested material splits into feces (→ fine_detritus), excretion (N→TAN, C→DOC), respiration (C→DIC, O2 demand with O2-limited scaling), and retained (→ microfauna.reserve_g). Added 4 new routing parameters to ProcessParams, a reserve_g field to MicrofaunaState, updated N/C budget component arrays (17→18, 14→15), and wrote 8 tests covering conservation, TAN/DO fluxes, and proportionality.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Added microfauna routing parameters to ProcessParams (microfauna_assimilation_efficiency, microfauna_respiration_fraction_of_assimilated, microfauna_excretion_fraction_of_assimilated, microfauna_growth_fraction_of_assimilated) with serde defaults and default functions matching shrimp Phase-1 values (0.50, 0.70, 0.10, 0.20).
2. [Completed] Added reserve_g field to MicrofaunaState in biology.rs as the explicit 'retained' destination required by the routing contract. Field is serde-defaulted to 0.0 and included in the Default impl.
3. [Completed] Updated nitrogen_budget_components (17→18) and carbon_budget_components (14→15) in budget.rs to include microfauna.reserve_g. Updated the BudgetSnapshot struct array sizes to match.
4. [Completed] Rewrote microfauna.rs: replaced route_algae_loss_to_dissolved_organics and route_detritus_loss_to_dissolved_organics with a proper route_consumed_food function implementing the consumer routing contract. Feces→fine_detritus, excretion N→TAN + alkalinity, excretion C→DOC, respiration C→DIC with O2-limited scaling, respiration N→TAN + alkalinity, retained→microfauna.reserve_g. Added O2_PER_MG_C_RESPIRED and MG_N_PER_MEQ_AMMONIA constants.
5. [Completed] Updated budget_tracking.rs: added microfauna.reserve_g to is_shared_budget_path discovery rules and to manual total_n/total_c sum tests.
6. [Completed] Created microfauna_routing.rs test file with 8 tests: fraction validity, closed-system N conservation (7-day run via step_and_inspect), closed-system C conservation (7-day run), single-step N+C conservation, TAN increase from feeding, DO decrease from feeding, proportionality of TAN/DO to population_index, and DIC/feces/reserve generation.
7. [Completed] Ran cargo test (all 270+ tests pass), cargo clippy (clean), cargo fmt --check (clean).

## Validation Evidence

- All 8 microfauna_routing tests pass: fraction sums valid, closed-system N conservation (0.01 mg tolerance over 168 hours), closed-system C conservation (0.01 mg tolerance over 168 hours), single-step N+C conservation (1e-6 tolerance), TAN increase, DO decrease, proportional TAN/DO scaling, DIC/feces/reserve generation
- All 22 budget_tracking tests pass including test_budget_component_labels_cover_all_element_bearing_fields (structural coverage test now discovers microfauna.reserve_g), test_total_n_helper_sums_all_pools, test_total_c_helper_sums_all_pools, test_closed_system_n_conservation, test_closed_system_c_conservation
- All 8 shrimp_feeding_pathway tests continue to pass (no regressions in shrimp routing)
- All 13 shrimp_population tests pass including microfauna_suppression_under_heavy_grazing
- cargo clippy produces zero warnings, cargo fmt --check passes

## Outstanding Risks

- microfauna.reserve_g grows without bound since there is no decay/death drain for microfauna reserve — acceptable in Phase 1 per ROUTING.md ('their retained share may stay approximate until a later biomass-backed model exists') but should be addressed when a biomass-backed microfauna model is implemented
- The new reserve_g field uses serde(default) for backward compatibility with existing save files; however the save_load migration tests should be verified if save schema version checking is strict — current tests pass so this appears safe
- Microfauna routing parameters use the same default values as shrimp (0.50/0.70/0.10/0.20) which is a reasonable starting point but may warrant tuning for ecological accuracy in later phases
